title: Throughput SLA Fabric: policy layer and graceful spillover for regional dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a policy-driven Throughput SLA Fabric (TSF) that enforces customer throughput guarantees across regional and multi-zone dedicated fleets while enabling graceful spillover and respecting data residency constraints. The TSF will act as a runtime policy layer that: (1) maps SLA commitments to capacity slices, (2) coordinates autoscale/prewarm and spillover decisions, and (3) enforces residency circuit-breakers to prevent cross-jurisdiction failovers when required.
background: Customers committing to reserved/dedicated capacity expect predictable throughput and isolation. Existing prewarm and burst models are single-region and ad-hoc for spillover. Operators currently lack a unified policy surface that ties SLA contracts, autoscale behavior, and residency guardrails together. This has resulted in either over-provisioning or opaque failover that can violate residency requirements.
proposal: Design a TSF service with three main components: 1) Contract Mapper: consumes commitment metadata (region scope, committed TPS/throughput, soft-window for spillover) and materializes persistent capacity slices. 2) Orchestrator/Decision API: evaluates live metrics (queue depth, token/sec, tail latency) against tenant SLOs and decides: scale-up in-region, prewarm spillover region(s), or throttle/queue. 3) Residency Policy Engine: a ruleset that evaluates jurisdiction constraints and toggles allowed spillover targets; includes an emergency 'residency circuit-breaker' mode to block cross-border transfers entirely.
config_schema_examples:
Example dedicated config fields (YAML in Console/API):
- commitment_scope: regional
- committed_qps: 2500
- spillover_policy: staged -> ['same-continent', 'explicit-allow-list']
- spillover_window_ms: 30000
- preemptibility: optional|required|none
- residency: { allowed_regions: ['eu-west-1'], forbid_cross_border: true }
(This will be codified in our API contract and Console UI.)
autoscale_policies: We will support three autoscale profiles initially: 1) Occupancy SLO: auto-scale when GPU occupancy > threshold for X seconds. 2) Latency SLO: scale when 95th percentile tail token latency breaches SLO. 3) Commitment-backed: maintain a warm reserve sized to committed throughput with predictive prewarm windows based on historical diurnal patterns. Policies are pluggable; customers can select or supply custom policy hints.
spillover_strategy: Graceful spillover must prioritize: local in-region capacity, same-country spillover (if allowed), same-continent, then explicit allow-list regions. Spillover is staged with a ramp (e.g., 10/30/60s steps) and prefers model-compatible variants (quantized or CPU-fallback) if full-capacity nodes unavailable. Spillover must record a residency decision trace to the request ID for auditing.
residency_guardrails: Residency rules are declarative: forbid_cross_border, allow_listed_regions, data_tagging (per-request). The runtime enforcement includes: (a) request-level header propagation for residency tags, (b) route validation in Orchestrator, and (c) a hard-circuit mode that returns 409/451 when an inbound request would violate policy. All decisions logged to audit stream.
acceptance_criteria:
- TSF can ingest commitments for a test customer and materialize capacity slice(s).
- Orchestrator recommends scale decisions in a simulation run with synthetic load that meets expected behavior for occupancy and latency policies.
- Residency circuit-breaker prevents spillover in a controlled canary and returns clear error codes.
- Console shows per-commitment trace of spillover decisions and cost delta estimate.
- End-to-end integration test covering prewarm -> spillover -> rollback under load.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Unintended cross-border failover due to race during drain. Mitigation: implement staged drain handshake + local prewarm with residency tagging and block phase when circuit open.
- Risk: Cost blowup from over-aggressive prewarm. Mitigation: cost-guard spec in policy with hard budget cap and TTL on prewarm nodes.
- Risk: Oscillation between regions. Mitigation: hysteresis rules and cooldown windows in Orchestrator.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal sim environment (2 weeks): stress TSF simulator with recorded production traces. 2) Canary customers (3 customers, non-residency sensitive) in single region with observability and kill-switch. 3) Expand to multi-zone within region, add residency circuit-breaker tests with legal. 4) GA with Console controls and audit logs. Each phase is gated by performance, correctness, and legal sign-off.
observability_and_metrics: Expose metrics per-commitment: allocated_capacity, used_capacity, spillover_count, spillover_latency, residency_block_count, prewarm_cost_estimate. Add traces that link request->orchestrator-decision->target-node and a dashboard for top spillover consumers.
testing_and_e2e:
- Unit tests for Contract Mapper and Residency Engine.
- Integration test: deploy TSF to staging and replay traffic captured from dedicated pools.
- Chaos test: simulate regional failure and validate spillover behavior and circuit-breaker enforcement.
- Load tests to validate tail latency SLOs under committed throughput.
migration_notes: Existing dedicated customers without explicit commitments default to current autoscale behavior. We will provide a one-click migrate flow in Console to create a TSF commitment entry from existing reserved config, with a 30-day opt-out window. A migration script will reconcile billing tags for prewarm cost attribution.
open_questions: How granular should commitments be (per-tenant vs per-route)?
What is the default spillover window and how much hysteresis is acceptable for customer UX?
Do we support mixed-residency commitments (some requests allowed cross-border, others not) at per-route level?
